experiment: Phase 6.2 - harm-associated SAE feature discovery and multi-feature probe

splits.note: Deduplicated by normalized response text before splitting; discovery/validation/test are non-overlapping

single_feature.selection_method: Highest absolute Cohen's d on discovery split (finite, prevalence-filtered)

test_set_results.note: Threshold selected on validation to maximize F1, not explicitly targeting a fixed recall

single_feature.qualitative_finding: Fires on ~99% of both harmful and safe held-out text (near-universal activation); top OpenWebText examples show generic formatting/structural text, not coherent harm semantics. Likely a broad, confounded feature rather than a clean harm detector.

multi_feature_probe.feature_selection: Top N finite features by absolute Cohen's d on discovery split only; sanity-checked to reproduce feature #3149's known validation AUROC (0.6512) before trusting results

finding: A 100-feature regularized linear probe improved AUROC from 0.653 (single feature) to 0.796 on a genuinely untouched holdout, reducing false positives by ~23.6 percentage points at comparable recall. This indicates harm-related signal is distributed across multiple SAE features rather than concentrated in one monosemantic feature.
limitations: Evaluated on BeaverTails response text only; not tested against paraphrased, indirect, or fictional harmful content
No raw-residual or plain-text-classifier (e.g. TF-IDF) baseline evaluated
60.8% false positive rate on the final holdout is operationally unacceptable for a deployable monitor
96 of 100 selected coefficients are nonzero - a regularized probe, not a sparse one
